finding.claim: Unauthenticated /fetch passes the attacker-supplied target query parameter directly to http.Get with no scheme, host, IP-range, port, or redirect validation, and streams the full response body back to the caller.
finding.source: main.go:15 r.URL.Query().Get("target") on GET /fetch (registered at main.go:41)

trace.note: http.HandleFunc("/fetch", fetch) registers the unauthenticated route
target read from query string, attacker-controlled
http.Get(target) issues the outbound request with no validation
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the full response to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: None on this path. No allowlist, no url.Parse, no private/loopback/link-local IP check, no port restriction, no CheckRedirect. Go's http.Get only accepts http/https schemes, so reachable surface is HTTP(S) to any internal host (e.g. 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254).

verdict.guard_found: none. The allowlist map at main.go:9-12 and the hostname check at main.go:27 exist only in safeFetch (main.go:25-38), which is registered at main.go:42. The /fetch path (main.go:14-23, registered at main.go:41) has no validation before http.Get at main.go:16.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled query value at main.go:15 flows unvalidated into http.Get at main.go:16 and the full body is returned via io.Copy at main.go:22, with the only allowlist guarding a different handler (safeFetch, main.go:27) that is not the route on /fetch (main.go:41).

finding.claim: /safe checks the allowlist only on the initial URL (main.go:27). http.Get follows redirects to any host by default, so an allowlisted host that returns a 3xx to an internal address causes the server to fetch the internal target and return its body.
finding.source: main.go:26 r.URL.Query().Get("target") on GET /safe (registered at main.go:42)

trace.note: http.HandleFunc("/safe", safeFetch) registers the unauthenticated route
allowed[u.Hostname()] check on first hop only; fails closed on parse error, userinfo tricks, and case/trailing-dot variants
http.Get on allowed host; default client follows up to 10 redirects with no CheckRedirect, so Location may point to any host
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) returns the final-hop body to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: url.Parse error check (main.go:27, fail-closed). u.Hostname() allowlist lookup (main.go:27) on first hop only. Port is not restricted but host is still allowlisted, so not reported separately. No CheckRedirect, no per-hop validation, no dial-time IP filtering. Exploitability depends on an open redirect or attacker-influenced 3xx on images.example.org or docs.example.org, which lives outside this repo and was not verified.

verdict.guard_found: Exact map membership on u.Hostname() at main.go:27 (allowed[...], fails closed on parse error). This runs only on the initial URL. No CheckRedirect, per-hop check, or dial-time IP filter exists anywhere in main.go, so it does not stop a 3xx from an allowlisted host to an internal address.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches main.go: route at :42, handler at :25, attacker-controlled target at :26, first-hop allowlist at :27, http.Get at :31 with default redirect following, and body copied back at :37. The allowlist check at :27 is a closing guard only for the first hop, and nothing at :31 or in the handler validates redirect targets, so the redirect bypass holds. Exploitation still depends on an open redirect or attacker-influenced 3xx on images.example.org or docs.example.org, which is outside this repo and unverified. Separately, the unauthenticated /fetch handler at main.go:16 is a direct, unguarded SSRF that the candidate did not report.
